## Ingredients

- [ ] 1 store-bought pie crust (9-inch), thawed if frozen
- [ ] 5 large eggs
- [ ] 1 cup heavy cream (or half-and-half)
- [ ] 1/2 cup milk
- [ ] 6 slices bacon, cooked and crumbled
- [ ] 1 1/2 cups broccoli florets, steamed and chopped
- [ ] 1 cup gruyere, shredded
- [ ] 1/2 tsp salt
- [ ] 1/4 tsp black pepper
- [ ] Pinch of nutmeg (optional)

## Instructions

1. Preheat oven to 375°F. Par-bake the store-bought crust per package directions if it calls for it (or blind bake with pie weights 8-10 minutes) to help prevent a soggy bottom. Let cool slightly.
2. Cook the bacon in a skillet until crisp. Drain on paper towels and crumble.
3. Steam or blanch the broccoli florets until just tender-crisp, 2-3 minutes. Drain well, pat dry, and roughly chop.
4. Whisk together the eggs, cream, milk, salt, pepper, and nutmeg (if using) until smooth.
5. Scatter the bacon, broccoli, and gruyere evenly over the bottom of the crust. Pour the egg mixture on top.
6. Bake 35-45 minutes, until the center is just set (no longer jiggly) and the top is golden. Tent with foil partway through if the crust browns too fast.
7. Let rest 10 minutes before slicing.

## Notes


A 9-inch quiche naturally cuts into 6-8 wedges — "Serves 4" here just means hearty slices for a family meal, cut smaller for more servings.

data.name: Za'atar Lamb Chops with Mint Sauce

body: ## Ingredientsn### Mint marinade & sauce (makes a double batch — half marinates, half stays fresh to serve)n- [ ] 1 cup fresh mint leavesn- [ ] 1/2 cup olive oiln- [ ] 1 tbsp sugarn- [ ] 3 tbsp sherry vinegar (or red wine vinegar)n- [ ] 1 shallot, choppedn- [ ] 2 tbsp garlic, mincedn- [ ] 1/2 tsp saltnn### Lambn- [ ] 8 lamb rib or loin chopsn- [ ] 2 tbsp za'atarn- [ ] 1 tsp saltn- [ ] 1/2 tsp black peppernn### To serven- [ ] Tzaziki, optionalnn## Instructionsn1. Blend the mint, olive oil, sugar, vinegar, shallot, garlic, and salt (food processor or immersion blender) until mostly smooth — a few flecks of mint are fine.n2. Set aside half the mixture, covered, in the fridge to use later as a fresh finishing sauce (it never touches raw lamb, so it's food-safe to spoon over the cooked chops).n3. Rub the lamb chops with za'atar, salt, and pepper, then toss with the remaining half of the mint mixture to coat. Cover and refrigerate at least 4 hours, up to overnight.n4. Remove the chops from the fridge 20-30 minutes before cooking to take the chill off.n5. Sear in a hot skillet or grill over medium-high heat, about 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare (or to your liking).n6. Let rest 5 minutes. Spoon the reserved mint sauce over the chops and serve, optionally with tzaziki on the side.nn## NotesnSwapped the British-style vinegar mint sauce for a Middle Eastern mint marinade that doubles as the sauce — blended fresh with olive oil, shallot, and garlic, split before it touches the raw lamb so half stays food-safe to serve. Pairs well with [Tzaziki](https://app.notion.com/p/3dc72417c053817db939dd1e49eb960a) as an alternate/additional condiment — that recipe is elsewhere in this database.

## Ingredients


### Brussels sprouts

- [ ] 1.5 lbs brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved
- [ ] 1 tbsp neutral oil
- [ ] Salt, to taste

### Fragrant sauce

- [ ] 1 tbsp minced ginger
- [ ] 1 tsp sesame oil
- [ ] 1/4 tsp salt
- [ ] 2 tbsp oyster sauce
- [ ] 2 tbsp chili crunch
- [ ] 1 tbsp sugar
- [ ] 1 tbsp fried garlic
- [ ] 2 tbsp soy sauce
- [ ] 1 tsp fish sauce
- [ ] 1/4 cup water
- [ ] 1 tbsp chili oil
- [ ] 1 tsp sichuan oil
- [ ] 1 tbsp black vinegar (added at the end)

### To finish

- [ ] Cilantro, chopped
- [ ] Scallions, sliced
- [ ] Thai chilis, chopped
- [ ] Tiger Aioli, to drizzle (optional)

## Instructions

1. Toss the brussels sprouts with the neutral oil and a pinch of salt. Air fry at 400°F for 12-15 minutes, shaking the basket halfway through, until crispy and charred in spots.
2. Meanwhile, make the sauce: combine the ginger, sesame oil, salt, oyster sauce, chili crunch, sugar, fried garlic, soy sauce, fish sauce, water, chili oil, and sichuan oil in a small saucepan.
3. Bring to a simmer and cook, stirring occasionally, until it reduces to a nappe consistency (thick enough to coat the back of a spoon), about 5-8 minutes.
4. Remove from heat and stir in the black vinegar. Let cool slightly.
5. Toss the hot brussels sprouts with the sauce, cilantro, scallions, and thai chilis.
6. Drizzle with Tiger Aioli if using, and serve immediately.

## Notes


Pairs with [Tiger Aioli](https://app.notion.com/p/3dc72417c05381c6a136d14d0107ed05) as an optional drizzle. 


"Nappe" just means the sauce has reduced enough to coat the back of a spoon without running right off.

## Ingredients

- [ ] 2 lbs boneless chicken thighs
- [ ] 1/2 cup plain Greek yogurt
- [ ] 3 tbsp lemon juice
- [ ] 3 tbsp olive oil
- [ ] 4 garlic cloves, minced
- [ ] 2 tsp ground cumin
- [ ] 2 tsp smoked paprika
- [ ] 1 tsp ground coriander
- [ ] 1/2 tsp ground turmeric
- [ ] 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon
- [ ] 1/4 tsp ground cloves
- [ ] 1 1/2 tsp salt
- [ ] 1/2 tsp black pepper
- [ ] Pita bread, warmed, to serve
- [ ] Tzaziki, to serve
- [ ] Tomato/Onion Mix, to serve

## Instructions

1. Whisk together the yogurt, lemon juice, olive oil, garlic, cumin, paprika, coriander, turmeric, cinnamon, cloves, salt, and pepper.
2. Coat the chicken thighs thoroughly in the marinade. Cover and refrigerate at least 2 hours, up to overnight for best flavor.
3. Cook: sear in a hot skillet or grill 5-7 minutes per side until charred and cooked through (165°F internal), or roast at 425°F for 20-25 minutes, or thread onto skewers and grill.
4. Let the chicken rest 5 minutes, then slice thin against the grain.
5. Warm the pita bread. Assemble with sliced chicken, tzaziki, and tomato/onion mix.

## Notes


See [Tzaziki](https://app.notion.com/p/3dc72417c053817db939dd1e49eb960a) and [Tomato/Onion Mix](https://app.notion.com/p/3dc72417c0538183a151e2ac2e6e02e4) for the accompanying condiment and side — both are their own recipes in this database since they're reusable beyond shawarma night.

## Ingredients

- [ ] 1/2 cup unsalted butter, melted
- [ ] 1 cup granulated sugar (or 3/4 cup brown sugar, for more moisture)
- [ ] 1 large egg
- [ ] 1 tsp vanilla extract
- [ ] 1 cup mashed ripe banana (about 2-3 bananas, the spottier the better)
- [ ] 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
- [ ] 1 tsp baking soda
- [ ] 1/2 tsp salt
- [ ] 1 cup chocolate chips, divided

## Instructions

1. Preheat oven to 350°F. Grease a 9x13-inch pan.
2. Whisk together the melted butter and sugar. Beat in the egg and vanilla, then stir in the mashed banana.
3. Fold in the flour, baking soda, and salt until just combined — don't overmix.
4. Fold in most of the chocolate chips, reserving 2 tbsp to sprinkle on top.
5. Spread the batter into the pan and scatter the reserved chocolate chips over the top.
6. Bake 25-30 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
7. Cool before slicing.

## Notes


Use very ripe, brown-spotted bananas for the best flavor.

## Ingredients

- [ ] 1 cup Greek yogurt
- [ ] 1/2 cucumber, grated and squeezed dry
- [ ] 1 garlic clove, minced or grated
- [ ] 1 tbsp lemon juice
- [ ] 1 tsp za'atar
- [ ] 1/2 tsp salt
- [ ] 1 tbsp olive oil, plus more to drizzle

## Instructions

1. Grate the cucumber, toss with a pinch of salt, and let sit 10 minutes. Squeeze out the excess liquid in a clean towel or cheesecloth.
2. Combine the squeezed cucumber with the yogurt, garlic, lemon juice, za'atar, and salt.
3. Stir in the olive oil.
4. Chill at least 30 minutes for the flavors to meld. Drizzle with a little more olive oil before serving.

## Notes


Made as a condiment to go with the Shawarma with Pita Bread, but works with grilled meats or veggies generally.

## Ingredients

- [ ] 2 cups cherry tomatoes, halved
- [ ] 1/4 red onion, thinly sliced
- [ ] 2 tbsp olive oil
- [ ] 1 tbsp red wine vinegar
- [ ] 1/2 tsp salt
- [ ] 1/2 tsp Aleppo pepper
- [ ] Handful Italian parsley

## Instructions

1. Toss the cherry tomatoes and red onion together in a bowl.
2. Add the olive oil, red wine vinegar, salt, Aleppo pepper, and chopped up parsley. Toss to coat.
3. Let sit 10-15 minutes so the flavors meld before serving.

## Notes


Made as a side to go with the Shawarma with Pita Bread.

## Ingredients


### Crust

- [ ] 1 cup (2 sticks) unsalted butter, softened
- [ ] 1/2 cup granulated sugar
- [ ] 2 cups all-purpose flour
- [ ] 1/4 tsp salt

### Filling

- [ ] 4 large eggs
- [ ] 1 1/2 cups granulated sugar
- [ ] 1/3 cup all-purpose flour
- [ ] 2/3 cup fresh lemon juice (about 4-5 lemons)
- [ ] Zest of 2 lemons

### To finish

- [ ] Powdered sugar, for dusting

## Instructions

1. Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 9x13-inch pan with parchment, leaving an overhang on two sides.
2. Cream the butter and sugar, then mix in the flour and salt until a soft, crumbly dough forms.
3. Press the dough evenly into the bottom of the pan. Bake 18-20 minutes until lightly golden.
4. While the crust bakes, whisk together the eggs, sugar, flour, lemon juice, and zest until smooth.
5. Pour the filling over the hot crust and return to the oven. Bake 20-25 minutes, until the filling is just set (a slight jiggle in the center is fine).
6. Cool completely at room temperature, then chill 1-2 hours before cutting.
7. Lift out using the parchment overhang, dust with powdered sugar, and cut into bars.

## Notes


For cleaner cuts, wipe the knife between slices.

## Ingredients


### Crust

- [ ] 1 1/2 cups fine chocolate wafer crumbs (about 30 wafers) — or ground galletas María / digestive biscuits, see Carl's Notes
- [ ] 1/4 cup sugar
- [ ] 1/4 cup (1/2 stick) unsalted butter, melted

### Alternative crust (ginger-Oreo, no bake)

- [ ] 1/4 package Anna's ginger thins
- [ ] 16 Oreos
- [ ] 1/2 cup (1 stick) butter, melted

### Filling

- [ ] 1 1/2 tsp unflavored gelatin
- [ ] 1 1/3 cups well-chilled heavy cream, divided
- [ ] 1/4 cup sugar
- [ ] 1/4 cup green crème de menthe
- [ ] 1/4 cup white crème de cacao
- [ ] 4 large egg yolks
- [ ] Grated mint-flavored chocolate, for garnish

## Instructions

1. **Crust:** Stir together the wafer crumbs, sugar, and melted butter until well combined. Pat onto the bottom and up the side of a buttered 9-inch pie plate. Bake in the middle of a preheated 450°F oven for 5 minutes. Let cool completely.

    **Alternative crust:** Pulse the ginger thins and Oreos in a food processor into fine crumbs, then drizzle in the melted butter while processing until combined. Press into the pie pan — no baking needed.

2. Beat the egg yolks in a bowl and set aside.
3. In a metal bowl, sprinkle the gelatin over 1/3 cup of the cream and let it soften 5 minutes.
4. Whisk in the sugar, crème de menthe, and crème de cacao. Set the bowl over a saucepan of simmering water and cook, whisking constantly, until it registers 160°F on a candy thermometer. Remove from heat.
5. Temper the egg yolks: while stirring, add the hot mixture to the yolks a spoonful at a time, repeating about 7-8 times until the yolks are quite hot.
6. While stirring the hot mixture, pour the tempered yolks back in.
7. Set the bowl over a larger bowl of ice and cold water, and stir until the mixture is cooled and thickened.
8. In a separate bowl, beat the remaining 1 cup cream until it holds stiff peaks, then fold it thoroughly into the cooled crème de menthe mixture.
9. Pour the filling into the crust and chill at least 4 hours, or until set.
10. Sprinkle with grated mint chocolate before serving.

## Carl's Notes

- Make 1.5x or 2x the recipe for a large pie pan.
- In Costa Rica, Carl uses galletas María, ground up, instead of chocolate wafer crumbs. Digestive biscuits are another alternative.
- If there's no cocoa flavor in whatever crust cookie you're using (e.g. plain galletas María instead of chocolate wafers), just use brown sugar and perhaps a little honey to compensate.
- Bailey's has gone in sometimes, but it makes the green noticeably less green — beware.

## Notes


Recipe as passed down comes from a Usenet posting ([rec.food.recipes](http://rec.food.recipes/), Aug 2001) crediting Gourmet magazine, titled "Grasshopper Pie (Fit for a King)."

## Ingredients

- [ ] 2 tbsp oil
- [ ] 1/2 onion, diced
- [ ] 1/2 red bell pepper, diced
- [ ] 2 garlic cloves, minced
- [ ] 1 can (15 oz) black beans, drained (reserve the liquid)
- [ ] 3 cups day-old cooked rice (cold, from the fridge)
- [ ] 2-3 tbsp Salsa Lizano, plus more to taste
- [ ] 1/4 cup cilantro, chopped
- [ ] Salt, to taste

## Instructions

1. Heat oil in a large skillet or wok over medium heat. Sauté onion and bell pepper until softened, about 5 minutes. Add garlic and cook 1 minute more.
2. Add the drained black beans along with a splash (2-3 tbsp) of the reserved bean liquid. Lightly mash some of the beans with the back of the spoon.
3. Add the day-old rice, breaking up any clumps, and stir-fry until everything is heated through and the rice takes on a light brown color from the beans, 5-8 minutes.
4. Stir in the Salsa Lizano and toss to coat evenly.
5. Remove from heat, fold in the cilantro, and season with salt to taste.
6. Serve as a breakfast staple with fried eggs, fried ripe plantains, and extra Salsa Lizano at the table.

## Notes


Day-old, fridge-cold rice is key — fresh rice turns mushy in the pan.

## Ingredients

- [ ] 3 tbsp chili crisp
- [ ] 1 tsp ginger, minced
- [ ] 2 tbsp aged Chinese black vinegar (Chinkiang)
- [ ] 1 tbsp oyster sauce
- [ ] 1 tsp sugar
- [ ] Pinch of salt, to taste (oyster sauce is already salty)
- [ ] 3 tbsp canola oil

## Instructions

1. Whisk all ingredients together in a bowl until combined.
2. Let sit for at least 10 minutes before serving so the flavors meld.
3. Use over noodles, dumplings, cold tofu, or grilled vegetables.

## Notes


Keeps refrigerated for 1-2 weeks; the oil may solidify slightly when cold, so let it come to room temp before serving.

## Ingredients

- [ ] 3 tbsp tamari
- [ ] 2 tbsp water
- [ ] 2 tbsp yuzu juice
- [ ] Zest of 1/2 lemon
- [ ] 1 tbsp lemon juice
- [ ] 1 scallion, thinly sliced
- [ ] 1/2 Thai chili, thinly sliced (seeds removed for less heat)
- [ ] 1 tsp sugar
- [ ] Pinch of salt

## Instructions

1. Whisk together the tamari, water, yuzu juice, lemon zest, and lemon juice.
2. Stir in the scallion, Thai chili, sugar, and salt.
3. Let sit 10 minutes so the flavors meld before serving.

## Notes


Bright and citrusy — good over the Cucumber Salad or as a dip alongside dumplings.

## Ingredients

- [ ] 2 English cucumbers, smashed and torn into bite-size chunks
- [ ] 1 tsp salt, plus more to taste
- [ ] 1/2 cup mixed greens (herbs, scallions, snap peas — whatever's on hand), thinly sliced
- [ ] 1/4 cup cilantro, chopped
- [ ] 2 tbsp yuzu juice (or fresh lemon juice)
- [ ] 4 oz soft or silken tofu, cubed
- [ ] Chili oil, to garnish
- [ ] Fried garlic and onion, to garnish

## Instructions

1. Toss the smashed cucumber pieces with 1 tsp salt in a colander set over a bowl. Let drain 2-4 hours, or overnight in the fridge, to release excess liquid.
2. Shake off any remaining liquid from the cucumbers and transfer to a serving bowl.
3. Toss with the sliced greens, cilantro, and yuzu (or lemon) juice. Season with additional salt to taste.
4. Top with the cubed tofu, a drizzle of chili oil, and a scatter of fried garlic and onion.

## Notes


Pairs well with the Yuzu Vinaigrette for extra dressing, or the Chili Vinaigrette for more heat.

## Ingredients

- [ ] 2 cups maseca (masa harina)
- [ ] ~1.5 cups warm water
- [ ] 1/2 tsp salt
- [ ] 8 oz low-moisture mozzarella or queso Oaxaca, sliced or shredded (see note on queso turrialba)
- [ ] Oil, for frying

## Instructions

1. In a bowl, whisk the maseca and salt together. Add the warm water gradually, mixing (by hand or with a spoon) until you have a smooth, soft dough that doesn't crack at the edges — add a splash more water if needed.
2. Rest the dough, covered, for 10 minutes.
3. Divide into 8-10 equal balls. Press each one into a ~4-5 inch round, using a tortilla press lined with plastic, or by hand between two sheets of plastic/parchment.
4. Place a portion of cheese on one half of each round. Fold the dough over into a half-moon and press/crimp the edges to seal (wet your fingers with a little water if the dough resists sealing).
5. Heat about 1/2 inch of oil in a skillet to medium-high (350°F). Fry the empanadas in batches, about 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown.
6. Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

## Notes


Queso turrialba is a Costa Rican semi-hard cow's milk cheese that melts well but browns rather than stretches. Good substitutes are low-moisture mozzarella, queso Oaxaca, or queso quesillo — avoid fresh/wet mozzarella, which releases too much moisture when fried.

## Ingredients

- [ ] 400g dry black beans (soaked overnight, or quick-soaked)
- [ ] 2 liters water
- [ ] 1 bay leaf
- [ ] 1/4 sweet red pepper, finely diced
- [ ] 1/4 white onion, finely diced
- [ ] 3 garlic cloves, minced
- [ ] 2 stalks celery, diced
- [ ] 1/2 bunch cilantro, stems and leaves separated, chopped (reserve some leaves for garnish)
- [ ] 18g salt, plus more to taste
- [ ] 15-30ml oil (for sofrito)
- [ ] 4-6 eggs
- [ ] Ripe green plantain
- [ ] Salsa Lizano, to serve

## Instructions

1. Combine soaked beans, 2 liters water, and the bay leaf in a large pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer, partially covered, for about 1.5-2 hours until beans are tender.
    - NOTE: If you have a pressure cooker, this can be done in as little as 30 minutes, and you can start on the rest of the prep as soon as you start the pressure cooker.
2. About 30 minutes before the beans are done, heat oil in a skillet and sauté the onion, red pepper, cilantro, and garlic until soft and fragrant (5 minutes) — this is the sofrito.
3. Stir the sofrito into the pot along with most of the chopped cilantro. Simmer another 20-30 minutes so flavors meld.
4. Make the patacones:
    1. Heat a pan with a light layer of oil at the bottom.
    2. Cut green plantain into rounds, about half an inch.
    3. Press rounds with a tortilla press until flat but not wafer thin, they need to be able to maintain their shape in the pan.
    4. Cook until golden brown on both sides, lightly salting to taste.
    5. Let sit on paper towels to drain oil and set aside.
5. Season with the salt (start with 1 tbsp, adjust to taste). Remove the bay leaf before serving.
6. For a thicker, more traditional body, stick blend some or ladle 250-475ml of the soup into a blender, purée, and stir back in.
7. For the last 5 or so minutes of cooking:
    1. While stirring in a circular motion, drop eggs one at a time into the pot to boil, wait enough for the whites to set between eggs.
    2. Add patacones.
8. Ladle into bowls, top with the reserved cilantro, and serve with salsa lizano on the side for people to add to taste.

## Notes


Day-old beans taste even better — this is a great make-ahead soup.

## Ingredients

- [ ] 1 lb (450g) extra firm tofu, cubed
- [ ] 6 oz ground pork, beef, or chicken (whatever you have)
    - Or the equivalent woodear mushrooms, rehydrated and chopped if going vegeterian
    - Or a mix
- [ ] 2 tbsp neutral oil
- [ ] 2 tbsp hot bean sauce (doubanjiang)
- [ ] 1 tbsp dried fermented black bean paste (douchi)
- [ ] 1 tbsp ginger, minced
- [ ] 1 tbsp garlic, minced
- [ ] 2 tbsp preserved mustard tuber (zha cai), rinsed and minced
- [ ] 1 tsp whole Sichuan peppercorns, toasted and ground, plus more for garnish
- [ ] 1 cup water
- [ ] 1 tbsp tamari
- [ ] 1 tsp sugar
- [ ] 1-2 tbsp chili crisp
- [ ] 1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water (slurry)
- [ ] Scallion greens, chopped, to garnish

## Instructions

1. Bring a pot of salted water to a gentle simmer and blanch the tofu cubes for 2 minutes to firm them up and remove any bean-y taste. Drain gently and set aside.
2. Heat the oil in a wok or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the ground meat or mushroom and cook, breaking it up, until browned.
3. Push the meat aside and add the hot bean sauce, black bean paste, ginger, and garlic to the cleared space. Fry 1-2 minutes until fragrant and the oil turns red, then stir everything together.
4. Add the preserved mustard tuber; stir-fry 1 minute.
5. Pour in the water, tamari, and sugar. Bring to a simmer.
6. Gently slide in the tofu cubes and simmer 5 minutes, spooning the sauce over the top or stirring gently, trying to keep the tofu in tact.
7. Stir in the chili crisp. Drizzle in the cornstarch slurry in two additions, gently folding, until the sauce thickens to coat the back of a spoon.
8. Finish with ground Sichuan peppercorn and scallions. Serve immediately over rice.

## Notes


Don't skip blanching the tofu and stirring gently — that's what keeps the cubes from breaking apart into mush.

## Ingredients

- [ ] 2 lbs gold potatoes, halved or quartered, skins on or off
- [ ] 1 lb fresh Costa Rican/Argentinian chorizo, cut into rounds or separated from the casing, if any
    - Hot Italian sausage can be used as a substitute.
- [ ] 2-3 tbsp [achiote ](https://www.amazon.com/Los-Patitos-Achiote-Paste-7-4/dp/B07643KN7S)
    - Can be found on amazon, Los Patitos red container.
- [ ] 1 red bell pepper, diced
- [ ] 1/2 white onion, diced
- [ ] 2 garlic cloves, minced
- [ ] Cilantro, chopped, for garnish
- [ ] Salt, to taste

## Instructions

1. Boil the potatoes in salted water until fork-tender, about 12-15 minutes. Drain and set aside.
2. Heat a skillet over medium heat, toss in and roughly break chorizo or sausage up with a wooden spoon. Cook 6-8 minutes until browned and cooked through.
3. Stir in achiote, bell pepper and onion. Sauté 5 minutes until softened and just starting to turn golden. Add the garlic and cook 3 more minutes.
4. Add the drained potatoes to the skillet and gently toss everything together with the chorizo and sofrito until well combined and heated through. Season with salt.
5. Garnish with pico de gallo or cilantro and serve, traditionally alongside warmed corn tortillas or rice.

## Notes

- Make sure to use Costa Rican/Argentinian chorizo, which has a similar texture to Italian sausage. Mexican chorizo breaks apart too easily.

## Ingredients

- [ ] 3 tbsp tamari
- [ ] 2 tbsp rice vinegar
- [ ] 2 tbsp water
- [ ] 1 tsp sugar
- [ ] Pinch of salt
- [ ] Pinch of white pepper
- [ ] 1 tsp sesame oil
- [ ] 2 tbsp canola oil

## Instructions

1. Whisk all ingredients together until the sugar dissolves.
2. Taste and adjust salt/sugar balance.
3. Use as an all-purpose dressing for noodles, salads, or as a dumpling dip.

## Notes


A lighter, cleaner counterpart to the Chili Vinaigrette — good for pairing with the Cucumber Salad.

## Ingredients


### Filling

- [ ] 1 lb ground chicken (thigh meat preferred)
- [ ] 1 tbsp shaoxing wine
- [ ] 1.5 tbsp soy sauce
- [ ] 1 tsp fish sauce
- [ ] Zest of 1/2 lemon
- [ ] 1/4 tsp five spice powder
- [ ] 1/4 tsp white pepper
- [ ] 1/2 tsp salt
- [ ] 2-3 tbsp water, added gradually
- [ ] 1/4 tsp baking soda
- [ ] 1 tbsp tapioca starch
- [ ] 1 tbsp duck fat, melted
    - [ ] Chicken/pork fat will do
- [ ] 1 tsp sesame oil
- [ ] 2 scallions, minced
- [ ] 1 tbsp ginger, minced
- [ ] 2 cups kale, finely shredded, massaged with a pinch of salt and squeezed dry
- [ ] 1 tbsp canola oil
- [ ] 1 tsp sesame oil (second addition)
- [ ] 1 tbsp garlic, minced
- [ ] 1/2 tsp salt
- [ ] 1/2 tsp mushroom powder
- [ ] ~24 dumpling wrappers

### Dumpling sauce

- [ ] 3 tbsp light soy sauce
- [ ] 1 tsp ginger, minced
- [ ] Pinch of salt
- [ ] 1 tsp sugar
- [ ] 1.5 tbsp rice vinegar
- [ ] Pinch of white pepper
- [ ] 1/2 tsp sesame oil

## Instructions

1. In a large bowl, combine ground chicken with shaoxing wine, soy sauce, fish sauce, lemon zest, five spice, white pepper, and 1/2 tsp salt. Stir briskly in one direction.
2. Add the water 1 tbsp at a time, continuing to stir in one direction until fully absorbed and the mixture turns sticky and pasty.
3. Mix in the baking soda, tapioca starch, duck fat, and 1 tsp sesame oil.
4. Fold in the shredded kale, scallions, ginger, canola oil, second 1 tsp sesame oil, garlic, remaining 1/2 tsp salt, and mushroom powder until evenly distributed. Chill the filling 30 minutes.
5. Place about 1 tbsp of filling in the center of each wrapper. Wet the edge with water, fold, and pleat to seal.
6. **To pan-fry (potsticker style):** heat oil in a nonstick skillet, arrange dumplings flat-side down, sear 1-2 minutes until golden, add 1/3 cup water, cover, and steam 5-6 minutes. Uncover and let the water cook off until the bottoms crisp again.

    **To steam:** steam over boiling water 8-10 minutes.


    **To boil:** boil in batches until they float, about 5-6 minutes.

7. For the sauce, whisk together the light soy sauce, ginger, salt, sugar, rice vinegar, white pepper, and sesame oil. Serve alongside.

## Notes


Stirring the filling in one direction (not back and forth) develops the myosin protein and gives the filling its characteristic springy, sticky texture. Uncooked dumplings freeze well on a tray, then bag once solid.

## Ingredients

- [ ] 1 whole egg (room temperature)
- [ ] 1 tbsp hot bean paste (doubanjiang)
- [ ] 1/2 tsp mala spice blend
- [ ] 1 tsp sugar
- [ ] 1/2 tsp salt
- [ ] 1 tsp fish sauce
- [ ] 1 tbsp water
- [ ] Zest of 1/2 lemon
- [ ] 1 tbsp lemon juice
- [ ] 1 tsp rice vinegar
- [ ] 1 tbsp chili oil
- [ ] 3/4 cup canola oil

## Instructions

1. In a blender or tall cup (for an immersion blender), combine the egg, hot bean paste, mala spice, sugar, salt, fish sauce, water, lemon zest, lemon juice, and rice vinegar. Blend until combined.
2. With the blender running on low, slowly drizzle in the canola oil, then the chili oil, until the mixture emulsifies and thickens to a mayo-like consistency.
3. Taste and adjust salt, acid, or spice as needed.

## Notes


If the emulsion breaks, start a fresh egg yolk in a clean container and slowly drizzle the broken mixture into it to re-emulsify.

Great aioli for fries, egg rolls or drizzled over fragrant brussels sprouts.

## Ingredients

- [ ] 1 lb ground beef or Costa Rican/Argentinian chorizo
- [ ] 2 chayote squash, peeled and diced
- [ ] 1/2 onion, diced
- [ ] 2 garlic cloves, minced
- [ ] 1-2 cups beef stock
- [ ] 1/4 cup cilantro, chopped
- [ ] Salt, to taste
- [ ] 1 tbsp oil

## Instructions

1. Heat oil in a large pot or skillet over medium heat. Sauté the onion and garlic until translucent, about 3-4 minutes.
2. Add the ground meat and cook, breaking it up, until browned, about 5-7 minutes. Drain excess fat if needed.
3. Add the diced chayote and beef stock (enough to just cover). Bring to a simmer, then cover and cook 15-20 minutes until the chayote is tender.
4. Uncover and let any excess liquid reduce for a few minutes so the picadillo isn't soupy.
5. About 1 minute before done, stir in the cilantro to keep its flavor fresh. Season with salt to taste.
6. Serve with white rice, black beans and/or pico de gallo.

## Notes


Corn kernels and a diced red bell pepper are common additions if you want to bulk it out.

## Ingredients

- [ ] 1 whole egg (room temperature; use pasteurized if serving to anyone who avoids raw egg)
- [ ] 2 tbsp Chinese hot mustard, prepared
- [ ] 1 tbsp rice vinegar
- [ ] 1 tsp ginger purée
- [ ] 1/2 tsp salt
- [ ] 1 tsp brown sugar
- [ ] 1 tsp sesame oil
- [ ] 1 tbsp water
- [ ] 3/4 cup canola oil

## Instructions

1. In a blender or tall cup (for an immersion blender), combine the egg, hot mustard, rice vinegar, ginger purée, salt, brown sugar, and water. Blend until combined.
2. With the blender running on low, slowly drizzle in the sesame oil, then the canola oil, until emulsified and thick.
3. Taste and adjust salt, sweetness, or mustard heat as needed.

## Notes


Great alongside the dumplings, egg rolls or drizzled over cold sesame noodles.

## Ingredients


### Sauce

- [ ] 1/3 cup tahini
- [ ] 3-4 tbsp warm water, to loosen
- [ ] 3 tbsp soy sauce
- [ ] 2 tbsp rice vinegar
- [ ] 1.5 tbsp sugar
- [ ] 1/4 tsp salt
- [ ] 1/4 tsp white pepper
- [ ] 2 garlic cloves, grated or minced
- [ ] 1 tbsp canola oil
- [ ] 1 tbsp sesame oil
- [ ] 1-2 tsp chili oil, to taste

### Noodles & veggies

- [ ] 12 oz fresh wheat noodles (or dried)
- [ ] 1 tsp canola oil, to toss noodles
- [ ] Watermelon radish, julienned
- [ ] Snap peas, ends trimmed and thinly sliced
- [ ] Edamame, shelled
- [ ] Assorted other julienned fresh veggies as available (carrot, cucumber, scallion, etc.)

## Instructions

1. Whisk the tahini with the warm water in a bowl until smooth and pourable (tahini can seize up at first — keep whisking).
2. Whisk in the soy sauce, rice vinegar, sugar, salt, white pepper, garlic, canola oil, sesame oil, and chili oil. Adjust water for a pourable, dressing-like consistency.
3. Cook the noodles according to package directions. Drain and rinse thoroughly under cold water until fully cooled. Drain well and toss with 1 tsp canola oil to prevent sticking.
4. Toss the noodles with the sesame sauce until evenly coated.
5. Top with watermelon radish, snap peas, edamame, and any other fresh veggies. Drizzle with a little extra chili oil or sesame oil to finish.

## Notes


Sauce can be made ahead and keeps well refrigerated for several days — thin with a splash of water before tossing with noodles.
